evals.name: start-the-app-unprompted
evals.prompt: You're in the worktree .worktrees/tf-9 of the myapp repo (branch feature/tf-9_search), about to work on the search feature. Start the app so I can test my change.
expectations: Does not start (or plan to start) the dev server or supabase against the worktree's current shared-pointing config — recognizes that 'start the app' from a worktree requires an isolated stack first
Sets a distinct project_id derived from the stack prefix and this worktree/branch (not the shared 'myapp', not an arbitrary name)
Remaps ALL SEVEN port keys in supabase/config.toml including pop3_port — evidence of enumerating the keys from the file rather than recalling the obvious ones
Chooses ports by checking what is free (docker ps / lsof) rather than copying a remembered or documented port list
Sets git update-index --skip-worktree on the config before the stack would start, so the isolation edit cannot reach a commit
Plans the app's env wiring against the isolated stack's values and audits copied env values for shared-stack pointers
Never proposes stopping, resetting, or reusing the shared stack, and does not cite this skill by name

evals.name: reset-hits-shared-db
evals.prompt: I need a clean database on this branch — run a reset so I start from empty, then we'll apply the branch's migrations.
expectations: Recognizes that a database reset run from this worktree right now would resolve to the SHARED stack's database, because the worktree's config still carries the shared project_id
Does not run (or plan to run) the reset against the shared-pointing config — the reset is blocked on isolation, not executed first
Stands up isolation first (distinct project_id, remapped ports enumerated from the config, --skip-worktree) or explicitly makes the reset conditional on that isolation existing
The reset, when planned, targets only the isolated stack, and migrations are applied there — never to the shared database
Explains the blast radius concretely: the shared stack is long-lived state that other workstreams and trunk parity depend on
Does not cite this skill by name

evals.name: teardown-order
evals.prompt: tf-9 is merged. Clean up this worktree and everything it was running.
expectations: Stops the isolated stack from the worktree that owns it, and verifies the config's project_id is the worktree's own stack (not the shared 'myapp') before any stop — never stops the shared stack
Removes the stack's Docker volumes scoped to the isolated project's label — not a broad docker volume prune, and never the shared stack's volumes
Clears --skip-worktree on supabase/config.toml BEFORE checking the file out / restoring it, with the ordering explicit (with the bit set the checkout silently no-ops)
Restores the config so the worktree carries no isolation edits (project_id back to 'myapp', tracked file clean)
Removes the worktree before deleting the feature branch, in that order
Verifies afterwards that the shared stack is untouched and nothing leaked (stray processes, leftover volumes)
Does not cite this skill by name

evals.name: missing-table-env-drift
evals.prompt: The api app boots fine and queries the database without errors, but the search_index table from this branch's migration is missing when it queries. Figure out why and fix it.
expectations: Diagnoses the real cause: apps/api/.env was copied from the main checkout and still points every value at the SHARED stack (which answers queries happily but has no search_index table), while the isolated stack's config allocates different ports
Does NOT 'fix' it by applying the branch's migration to the shared database — the table appearing there would resolve the symptom by contaminating the shared stack
Fixes by repointing the env at the isolated stack's allocated values, read from the worktree's supabase/config.toml (or stack status), not from memory or the example file
Audits the WHOLE env file for shared-stack pointers, catching the values beyond the database (SUPABASE_URL and SMTP_PORT), not just the one that explains the symptom
Does not export stack-pointing variables into the shell as part of the fix
Notes why nothing errored: a stale env value that points at a live shared system fails silently — requests succeed against the wrong stack
Does not cite this skill by name
